note: How the factory reads which build a stand runs (t-300). Closed variety lives here, never in code (FR-13): the methods a registry row may name and the parameter each needs, the order the probe tries them in when no row says otherwise, the default label and the default path, every limit, and the words a person reads for each outcome. A project brings a method this table does not hold by recording a `command` row: open variety is the person's, not this file's. The question texts, answer tokens and executor templates of the build question are added here by the driver node (N1b); nothing in the probe reads them.
registry_note: How the factory reads which build each stand runs, per stand and test profile. One file for all stands; the last row of a stand+profile is in force, earlier rows are history. Written by stand_identity.py and runtime_probe.py; commit it so the team shares it.
application_roles_note: The `implementation_repos[].role` words that name the repository a profile's stand RUNS (read by runtime_probe.pick_checkout when two repositories name one profile). Exact match, case counts. A role outside this list (tests, review) is never chosen over another repository; a project that spells its application role otherwise adds the word here or passes --checkout.

docker_failures.note: How a failed `docker exec` is told apart (t-345 F2), by the exit code and what docker said, lower-cased: `down` is a daemon that is unreachable or a container that is not running (nobody can answer it: no question); `tool_missing` is an image with no shell or no tool in it (a distroless image), which says nothing about the build; `file_missing` is a file that is not in the container. Anything else keeps the old road (`down`).
down: cannot connect to the docker daemon

non_runtime_files.note: Files that are not part of the running application (FB-8): a build or repository file the image never ships. Absent from the container such a file is recorded and not compared (a stale-build verdict would be false); present in the container it is compared like any other. Closed variety, so it is data (FR-13). A pattern without a slash matches the last path segment, a pattern with a slash the whole path of the diff; case-sensitive (fnmatch). A project adds names with `execution.non_runtime_files.also` and keeps its own application files compared with `execution.non_runtime_files.except` (`except` wins). A code file is never non-runtime, whatever a pattern says.

Which variant is asked is chosen by FIELDS of the probe's record (`result`, `asks_person`, `differing_files`, `deployed_source_revision`), never by reading a sentence (FR-12); a record that carries `registry_error`, `registry_method_failed` or `voided` gets the matching prefix on top of its variant (FR-7: the text moves when the situation moved). answers.note: The closed answers to the build question (t-300 N1b): ONE line per answer, read by code - the form's `word`, then (per `arg`) what follows it. `arg`: none = nothing may follow; optional = a value may follow; required = a value must follow (else the person is asked again, naming the form); commit = a commit of the checkout may follow (it must be the one the answer is about, else the person is asked again once). `value` is the shape the value must have as a WHOLE (a regular expression, after the pair of quotes `peel_arg` takes off): a value that misses it is not read as this form, the whole answer goes to the conductor - never a registry row with prose as a label (t-366 F3). `peel_arg` strips a pair of quotes or backquotes round the value; a command is never peeled, and its value is the rest of the line. Anything else, in any language, is not read: it goes to the conductor with the key and this table (FR-12, FR-13). `runs` are the executor commands the driver runs ITSELF for the answer, in order, stopping at the first that fails (FR-48); a person is never shown them. Slots: {task} {stand} {profile} {revision} (this story's commit) {deployed} (the commit the stand was read to run) {content} (the fingerprint of the files that differed, for `test as is`) {image} {words} (the person's line, whole) {arg}. A `?--flag` followed by its value is dropped when the value is empty. `hold` means: write the words down and keep the question open (the story stops).
